description:
Organic blue chamomile oil is extracted from an annual plant with erected stems and alternate leaves divided in thin lashes, thicker and wider than those of Roman Chamomile, and 40 – 60 cm high. The oil is produced by water steam distillation with an average yield of 0.1%. This plant is native to the Balkans, and has been used in shampoos since the days of the Vikings, because it adds luster to the blond hair. It used to be cultivated in Hungary an exported to Germany to be distilled and used under tea form. Chamazulene, a strong anti-inflammatory compound, is produced during the distillation through the conversion of a sesquiterpene lactone called “Matricin”. It confers the characteristic blue color to the oil. The Oil is a deep blue liquid (sometimes viscous) with a strong medicinal, phenolic, sweet and fruity odor.  Its apple aroma is the characteristic fragrance in many herbal skin-care products, and it is the reason why this plant is called “Manzanilla” in Spain.  The high Bisabolol chemotypes are preferred for therapy and cosmetic uses, due to the activity of this sesquiterpene alcohol.

100% Pure, Natural & Therapeutic Grade Gardenia Essential Oil - 5ml to 1000ml

Botanical Name: Gardenia jasminoides.

Collection Method: Enfleurage.

Plant Part: Flowers.

Aromatic Description: It has a rich, sweet floral aroma.

Strength of Aroma: Medium.

Plant Family: Rubiaceae.

Common Name: Cape jasmine, danh-danh, gardenia radicans, cape jessamine, gandhraj.

Origin: India.

Gardenia jasminoides is the botanical name of Gardenia Essential Oil which is extracted from the flowers of Gardenia through enfleurage process in which flower petals are soaked in fat, which absorbs most of the aromatic constituents of the petals. Then the aromatic fat is washed with alcohol to dissolve the fragrant molecules into the alcohol. Finally, the alcohol is separated from the fat and allowed to evaporate, leaving behind the Gardenia absolute. It has a characteristic sweet aroma that sees it feature as an important ingredient in perfumery and aromatherapy. It is also referred to as "White Angel".

Directions for Use:

. Diffusion: Use three to four drops in the diffuser of your choice. . Topical use: Apply one to two drops to the desired area.

description:
Sandalwood has an admirable status in eastern history.

High-quality Sandalwood is used for Buddhist sculptures, producing Buddhist prayer beads, and is taken as the material in building temples.

It's also burnt to worship God.

It has the meaning of admiration to God and spirits, and it implies eternity.

Inside the temple when monks are meditating, they burn Sandalwood during meditation for better soaking in Zen status.

In the palaces of ancient China, Sandalwood was appreciated by the nobles, and taken as the material for the production of high-class furniture, utensils and musical instruments.

During important occasions and rituals, Sandalwood was burnt to scent the environment.

Sandalwood grows very slowly, it takes tens of years to grow the bullet, the center of the trunk, so as to be extracted for high-quality Sandalwood essential oil.

In India Ayurveda, it records the precious medicinal effects of Sandalwood essential oil.

Indians call Sandalwood the panacea (miraculous cure) left in the human world by the Gods. Besides this, it also has a beautiful name, liquid gold.

In the past, the major origin of Sandalwood was in east India. But due to overharvesting and illegal smuggling, the number of wild Sandalwood trees has dropped immensely.

At present, the Indian government has strict control over the export of Sandalwood essential oil.

Currently, the major place of production of Sandalwood is aggregated in Australia.

The Australian government has plantation plans and management for stabilizing quality. Consisting of multiple components, Sandalwood essential oil gets a richer scent over time, and now it's the major source of high-quality sandalwood.

Cyperus scariosus, also known as Cypriol, Nutgrass and by its Hindi name Nagarmotha, is a plant of the family Cyperaceae. It is a perennial herbaceous riverbed plant native to India's Madhya Pradesh state. It is one of the most invasive weeds known, having spread out to a worldwide distribution in tropical and temperate regions.

Ayurvedic physicians use the plant for medicinal purposes for fevers, digestive system disorders, dysmenorrhea, and other maladies. Modern alternative medicine recommends using the plant to treat nausea, fever, and inflammation; for pain reduction; for muscle relaxation and for many other disorders.

About GC/MS Testing

Gas Chromatography (GC) measures the constituents contained within a particular essential oil sample by plotting each constituent found within the sample onto a graph. Mass Spectrometry (MS) identifies each of these components and their percentages. This process is used to identify any adulteration of the essential oil tested, ensure the therapeutic benefits, and prevent safety issues.

description:
100% Pure, Natural & Therapeutic Grade Gardenia Essential Oil - 5ml to 1000ml

Botanical Name: Gardenia jasminoides.

Collection Method: Enfleurage.

Plant Part: Flowers.

Aromatic Description: It has a rich, sweet floral aroma.

Strength of Aroma: Medium.

Plant Family: Rubiaceae.

Common Name: Cape jasmine, danh-danh, gardenia radicans, cape jessamine, gandhraj.

Origin: India.

Gardenia jasminoides is the botanical name of Gardenia Essential Oil which is extracted from the flowers of Gardenia through enfleurage process in which flower petals are soaked in fat, which absorbs most of the aromatic constituents of the petals. Then the aromatic fat is washed with alcohol to dissolve the fragrant molecules into the alcohol. Finally, the alcohol is separated from the fat and allowed to evaporate, leaving behind the Gardenia absolute. It has a characteristic sweet aroma that sees it feature as an important ingredient in perfumery and aromatherapy. It is also referred to as "White Angel".

. Diffusion: Use three to four drops in the diffuser of your choice. . Topical use: Apply one to two drops to the desired area.

IMPORTANT: All of our products are for external use only.

Gardenia jasminoides is the botanical name of Gardenia Essential Oil which is extracted from the flowers of Gardenia through enfleurage process in which flower petals are soaked in fat, which absorbs most of the aromatic constituents of the petals. Then the aromatic fat is washed with alcohol to dissolve the fragrant molecules into the alcohol. Finally, the alcohol is separated from the fat and allowed to evaporate, leaving behind the Gardenia absolute. It has a characteristic sweet aroma that sees it feature as an important ingredient in perfumery and aromatherapy. It is also referred to as "White Angel".

. Diffusion: Use three to four drops in the diffuser of your choice. . Topical use: Apply one to two drops to the desired area.

What is Frankincense?

Many know of Frankincense as one of the plant-derived treasures, along with myrrh, given to the newborn Jesus in the New Testament. Its use in a religious context goes beyond Christianity, however. According to the Hebrew Bible, frankincense and myrrh were components of the holy incense ritually burned in Jerusalem’s sacred temples during ancient times.

Frankincense is derived from the sap from a specific variety of trees in the genus Boswellia. Harvests are done at various times and the more opaque resins are considered to be the best quality.

    The main chemical of Frankincense oil constituents of the essential oil are Limonene, Pinene, Borneol, Farnesol, Phellandrene, Myrcene, and other constituents. Essential Oils are highly concentrated aromatic extracts derived from plants through distillation of a variety of plant material. Aromatic plants can be extracted from the following plant material: grasses, leaves, flowers, needles, twigs, peel of fruit, wood and roots.

Essential oils, which are harvested from various plants parts by distillation, are composed of many different components. The chemical ingredients give to each essential oil the scent of the essence. Some of these components have more odor than others, but the totality of the components are the eponymous scent or odor of the plant. By the nature of heat or steam (heat) and subjecting the plant to steam distillation, the odor of the resultant essential oil is not exactly the odor of the living plant. Plant Therapy의 티트리 에센셜 오일은 개인 관리 제품과 멜라루카 제품을 찾는 모든 사람에게 훌륭한 추가 아이템입니다. 이 오일은 흠과 자극받은 피부에 놀라운 효과가 있습니다. 오일 몇 방울은 홍조를 완화하고 부드러움을 회복하며 햇빛에 과다 노출된 피부를 진정시키는 데 도움이 될 수 있습니다. 흠을 지우는 데에도 좋습니다. 티트리, 라벤더, 레몬의 동일한 부분을 좋아하는 식물 테라피 캐리어 오일 2TBSP와 혼합하여 피부 진정 연어를 만들어보세요. 그런 다음 우려 영역에 추가하십시오. 국소 부위에 바르려면 얼굴에 1%까지 희석하십시오. 또한 면역 체계를 지원합니다.

What is Frankincense?

Many know of Frankincense as one of the plant-derived treasures, along with myrrh, given to the newborn Jesus in the New Testament. Its use in a religious context goes beyond Christianity, however. According to the Hebrew Bible, frankincense and myrrh were components of the holy incense ritually burned in Jerusalem’s sacred temples during ancient times.

Frankincense is derived from the sap from a specific variety of trees in the genus Boswellia. Harvests are done at various times and the more opaque resins are considered to be the best quality.

    The main chemical of Frankincense oil constituents of the essential oil are Limonene, Pinene, Borneol, Farnesol, Phellandrene, Myrcene, and other constituents. Nebulizing diffusers don’t require dilution, but regular use in diffusers and use in custom blends or cleaning/body care products require water dilution or a carrier oil. description:
The Holly tree, also known as wintergreen, prefers habitats with fertile soil under wet climates.

It has leather-liked glossy and thick leaves with slightly serrated margins, white color cone-shape panicles, and the ripened fruit of it turns red with a fine, round shape.

Stories from non-official history tell that the wintergreen fruit gets its scarlet color from once being dipped in the blood of Jesus Christ.

It also stands firmly without withering even in winter storms and wins itself an image of eternity.

People from western cultures hang wintergreen wreaths as a symbol of the Christmas tree.

Besides its frequent appearance as a Christmas symbol, wintergreen is a main element in some commonly found methyl salicylate-containing household medication like green oil, White Flower Embrocation, and Mentholatun ointment.

The fruit of wintergreen has a high level of methyl salicylate, which almost every medication for traumatic injury contains. Even the well-known aspirin is a part of metabolic product from methyl salicylate.

Residents from North America drink wintergreen herbal tea to soothe illnesses like headaches, sore throats, and rheumatism.

But, one thing customers have to pay close attention is that the wintergreen essential oil is 100 percent pure extracted organic oil, and indicates the concentration of methyl salicylate contained is more than 90 percent. Drinking wintergreen essential oil directly has a great risk of causing acidosis or even being fatal.

As a result, the internal intake of wintergreen essential oil is unconditionally prohibited.

Oil Applications:

  • Direct Inhalation
    Put 3 or 4 drops of essential oil onto a tissue or handkerchief and gently inhale. Alternatively, simply inhale directly from the bottle.
  • Steam Inhalation
    Fill a large container with almost boiling water and add 4-5 drops of essential oil or essential oil blend. Lean over the bowl and breathe slowly and deeply for a few minutes until relief is felt. A towel may be placed over the head to help direct the vapors.
  • Vaporize/Diffuse
    For the Ultra Sonic Essential Oil Diffusers, add water to the internal chamber and add 4-8 drops of essential oil(s).
  • Bath
    Use 8 drops of essential oil per 10mls carrier oil to ensure the essential oils are dispersed throughout the water.

Essential oil is a natural product extracted from a single plant species. Not all plants produce essential oils, and in the plants that do, the essential oil may be found in the roots, stems, leaves, flowers, or fruits. Unique aromatic compounds give each essential oil its characteristic essence. Essential oils are concentrated plant extracts that retain the natural smell and flavor, or "essence," of their source.

When used properly essential oils and aromatherapy products are safe and effective for the entire family. 

Caution: Do not use during pregnancy.

description:
Essential oils are natural aromatic compounds found in the seeds, bark, stems, roots, flowers, and other parts of plants. They can be both beautifully and powerfully fragrant. If you have ever enjoyed the gift of a rose, a walk by a field of lavender, or the smell of fresh cut mint, you have experienced the aromatic qualities of essential oils. In addition to giving plants their distinctive smells, essential oils provide plants with protection against predators and disease and play a role in plant pollination.
Essential oils are non water-based phytochemicals made up of volatile aromatic compounds. Although they are fat soluble, they do not include fatty lipids or acids found in vegetable and animal oils. Essential oils are very clean, almost crisp, to the touch and are immediately absorbed by the skin.
In addition to their intrinsic benefits to plants and being beautifully fragrant to people, essential oils have been used throughout history in many cultures for their medicinal and therapeutic benefits. Modern scientific study and trends toward more holistic approaches to wellness are driving a revival and new discovery of essential oil health applications.

description:
Organic blue chamomile oil is extracted from an annual plant with erected stems and alternate leaves divided in thin lashes, thicker and wider than those of Roman Chamomile, and 40 – 60 cm high. The oil is produced by water steam distillation with an average yield of 0.1%. This plant is native to the Balkans, and has been used in shampoos since the days of the Vikings, because it adds luster to the blond hair. It used to be cultivated in Hungary an exported to Germany to be distilled and used under tea form. Chamazulene, a strong anti-inflammatory compound, is produced during the distillation through the conversion of a sesquiterpene lactone called “Matricin”. It confers the characteristic blue color to the oil. The Oil is a deep blue liquid (sometimes viscous) with a strong medicinal, phenolic, sweet and fruity odor.  Its apple aroma is the characteristic fragrance in many herbal skin-care products, and it is the reason why this plant is called “Manzanilla” in Spain.  The high Bisabolol chemotypes are preferred for therapy and cosmetic uses, due to the activity of this sesquiterpene alcohol.

description:
A unique aroma and flavor

Spearmint essential oil contains at least 50% carvone, a chemical compound that brings to the spearmint that so characteristic taste and odor. It is therefore natural that the main use of the spearmint essential oil is an aroma for the food, pharmaceutical, cosmetics and perfume industries.

At home, it is easy and safe to add the spearmint essential oil to homemade preparations such as beverages, syrups, desserts, cakes and household products.

Refreshing and relaxing

Spearmint essential oil is particularly recommended to treat nervousness, fatigue, stress, anxieties, emotional shocks and depression. Carvone and its refreshing effect stimulates brain activity. On the other hand, limonene and its relaxing properties help to relax nerves and muscles.

How to use

The healthiest way to use this essential oil is in diffusion, inhalation or olfaction. Strongly dilute the essential oil in water (10% maximum).

As with many essential oils, spearmint essential oil should not be used for long periods of time, maximum 15 days.

In massage, add 5 to 10 drops to a carrier oil, such as coconut oil or olive oil. Do not apply to a large part of the body. Do not apply undiluted directly to the skin.

Spearmint essential oil blends very well with peppermint, eucalyptus, citrus and basil essential oils.

Cyperus scariosus, also known as Cypriol, Nutgrass and by its Hindi name Nagarmotha, is a plant of the family Cyperaceae. It is a perennial herbaceous riverbed plant native to India's Madhya Pradesh state. It is one of the most invasive weeds known, having spread out to a worldwide distribution in tropical and temperate regions.

Ayurvedic physicians use the plant for medicinal purposes for fevers, digestive system disorders, dysmenorrhea, and other maladies. Modern alternative medicine recommends using the plant to treat nausea, fever, and inflammation; for pain reduction; for muscle relaxation and for many other disorders.

In ancient Greece and India, Fennel used to be a flavoring in cooking and a cure in medication.

After eating Fennel, people feel satiated, so Fennel is considered to have the effect of appetite suppression.

In ancient China, Fennel was recorded as a cure in the treatment of snake bites.

Indians at present still have the habit of chewing Fennel seeds for fresh breath and boosting digestion. Now, Fennel is taken as an essential for women after the delivery of a baby in many areas around the world.

It helps to smooth the breast glands and better breastfeeding.

Fennel essential oil is indispensable for women during their postpartum period.

There are 7 kinds of Fennel plant, the one used as seasoning for barbecue is Ziran, which is also named Cumin, it grows the smallest seeds among all species.

Besides this, there is Anis, Caraway, Dill, Star anise, Ajowan, and Sweet Fennel, which is widely used in curing Gynecological diseases.

Sweet Fennel has milder features than the others; its smell tends to give a hint of sweetness.

As a result, people call it Sweet Fennel Florence Fennel, which has a non-separable relationship with women.

description:
Our Peppermint Essential Oil (aceite de menta) is steam distilled from the Mentha Piperita plant, a plant native to Europe and the Middle East valued for centuries in medicines, dental preparations, liniments, cleaners, and cosmetics. The oil has a sweet, sharp, mint aroma. Undiluted, this oil has a very strong aroma.

Peppermint Oil is used to focus the mind, improve memory, and promote wakefulness without causing nervousness and anxiety associated with other stimulants like caffeine. It gives a cooling sensation and has a calming effect on the body, which can relieve sore muscles when used topically. Among its many aromatherapy benefits are unclogged sinuses, curbing hunger cravings, increased energy, improved concentration and focus, and allergy relief.

Each and every lot of our peppermint oil is tested by an independent laboratory to ensure the oil is free from contaminants, dilutants, synthetic and adulterations. The oil is certified pure and genuine, and the oil is high quality and true to its smell.

How to Use Peppermint Essential Oil
INHALATION - Add 5-10 drops of peppermint oil in your essential oil diffuser or bath to relax, to increase focus, and to reduce food cravings.

FOR SKIN AND HAIR - Dilute 10-12 drops of peppermint oil with your favorite carrier oil (coconut oil, almond oil) to create a great-smelling lotion safe for the skin.

FOR PAIN RELIEF - Blend 10% peppermint oil with your favorite carrier oil. This can be increased up to 30%. Use a rollerball to apply directly to target area, or dab it on with your fingers.

CAUTION: Never put undiluted peppermint oil directly on your skin.

About GC/MS Testing

Gas Chromatography (GC) measures the constituents contained within a particular essential oil sample by plotting each constituent found within the sample onto a graph. Mass Spectrometry (MS) identifies each of these components and their percentages. This process is used to identify any adulteration of the essential oil tested, ensure the therapeutic benefits, and prevent safety issues.

At RAINBOW ABBY, every batch of oil purchased from a distiller or distributor is tested with GC/MS and FDA / SGS 100% pure certifications. You can rest assured that all RAINBOW ABBY essential oils are pure and safe to use, and their health benefits are uncompromised.

description: When you tear a piece of basil or cut open a lemon, what you smell are terpenes, a wide and diverse group of organic compounds found in plants, fruits, and vegetables that make them smell and taste the way they do. Terpenes and terpenoids are the primary constituents of essential oils. They help plants attract insects for pollination and repel predators. Beyond their adaptive and evolutionary purposes, terpenes make your food smell and taste delicious, and some claim they have a wide range of therapeutic benefits, with each terpene being associated with unique effects. FDA evaluations of these claims are available online.  Terpenes are widely used throughout many industries around the world. Restaurants, bakers, and the like, use terpenes to add bold flavors to renowned confections. Cosmetics industry uses them to create perfumes and the scents found in soaps, shampoos, and lotions. Roughly 20,000 of these compounds reside in a category of essential oils referred to as terpenes. These organic agents are what give fruits, herbs, and flowers their own specific scent and flavor. Terpenes also create a synergistic alliance with compounds found in the human body as well as other chemicals within the plant, this union is know as the “entourage effect”, which magnifies the benefits of the plant’s components.
